profile.headline: Developer Relations Engineer
profile.summary:
Since 2016 I have been working at Meta as a Developer Relations Engineer on the Metaverse Content team, where I spend most of my time helping developers build more VR successful applications and supporting a wide range of issues related to building a new platform and improving the developer ecosystem whose businesses rely on us. Much of my day to day work involves working with external partners, which leads to cross functional problem solving with internal teams to build a better platform for everyone. I've learned how to deliver impact in a high pressure environment by relying on relationships built on trust and good communication.

This role has provided me a unique lens on the industry through my work with hundreds of publishing partners as they do their best to succeed in a sometimes difficult market, and I do my best to help them navigate their way to their goals. Through this work, I have been part of countless negotiations, design and product reviews, team evaluations, and even the occasional M&A process. This is in addition to a regular cadence of technical and design work related to VR that builds on my background as a game developer. Having spent much of my career as an engineer, these experiences have granted me a uncommon perspective and skillset which I deeply appreciate. 

Please check out my personal site http://www.cosky.com for more information about my background and past work.

positions.title: Owner / Indie Game Developer
positions.description:
Bounding Box Games is a part-time effort currently exploring new game designs and platforms including PC, XBox One, Android, iOS, VR, Unity3D and Unreal.

Member of ID@XBOX

Previously focused on games for XBox Live Indie Games and Windows Phone, several games were created between 2010 and 2014 using a custom C# XNA Engine which features:
• Content pipeline supports the articulated, animated, skinned, compound meshes with shared or unique shaders along with constrained physics bodies and other metadata. 
• Animation blending tree with many node types such as standard animation playback, game triggers, aim blending, procedural animations and more. 
• Character attachment system, for characters that hold weapons, backpacks and other items while at the same time being attached to a vehicle. Hats.
• Database driven inventory system, including nested containers, item sprites, crafting recipes, item health, item wear, and character equipment slot management. 
• Persistent mission system, including progress tracking and mid-mission serialization support.
• High performance key/value database system that provides serialization support for all game data.
• Streaming, GPU-generated open world voxel terrain engine which supports persistent player modification, peer to peer networking, and join-in-progress gameplay.
• Instanced rendering system for both skinned and standard models. 
• Rigid body physics support, including the ability to transition from animated skinned models into physically simulated, detached body parts which can be individually skinned meshes, posed to match the corresponding original bones. 
• Fully networked gameplay including animation synchronization and world state.
positions.insights: Skills: Version Control · Virtual Reality (VR) · Skilled Multi-tasker · Critical Thinking · Optimization · Creative Ideation · Unreal Engine · Technical Architecture

positions.title: Principal Software Engineer
positions.description:
War Commander: Rogue Assault, a MMORTS created with Unity3D for Android and iOS. 

My work tended to revolve around the client - rendering, optimizing, asset management and helping content authors get their designs and art squeezed into the tight constraints of the mobile platforms. Some specifics include:

• Generally responsible for client performance and rendering systems.
• Map rendering system which includes some complex HLSL shaders.
• Provide code hooks for the UI/UX team.
• Work with artists to ensure assets are tuned and optimized.
• Asset tiering system to support a wide range of platforms.
• Streamed asset bundle management systems.
• Memory diagnostics system to identify inefficient assets.
• Created a code injection based instrumentation system for identifying transient managed objects that were causing too much GC.
positions.insights: Skills: Version Control · Skilled Multi-tasker · Critical Thinking · Optimization · Creative Ideation · Cross-functional Collaborations · Coaching · Technical Architecture

positions.title: Senior Physics Programmer
positions.locationName: San Diego County, California, United States
positions.description:
Red Dead Redemption:
Physics pod lead, key point of contact for the team for all physics related issues. I worked with members across all disciplines to help plan, author, create and extend code and content to meet the needs of the game. Often tasked with debugging some of the hardest and mysterious bugs encountered during development. Implemented and delegated features within the pod as needed. 

• Vehicles - Player control. Simulation debugging, tuning, extensions. Entry/exit/ejection/steering animation systems. Asset review and tuning. Attachment point and curve logic. 
• Wagons - Physical sim of horses pulling wagons.
• Characters - Locomotion tuning, physical and shootable collider tuning and extensions. Integration with vehicles. Ragdoll tuning and optimization. Triggers and prop interaction. Synchronized weapon animations. 
• Trains and mine carts - Spline constrained movement, hitch articulation, audio events and tuning systems.
• Projectiles/Explosions - Optimizations, debugging and extensions.
• Water simulation - River content pipeline and simulation work to apply river current forces.
• Boat and raft player control and physics.
• Attachment curves - Ledge and ladder pipeline work and simulator changes necessary for moving platforms.
• Prop and environment asset review and optimization sessions with artists. 
• Worked with animators to configure complex animation state machines.
• Streaming asset tuning and debugging for props and environment.
• Low level physics debugging, optimizations and extensions.
• Scripting support - Provided script APIs for designers as needed.
• NPC random encounter system - Terrain analyzer procedurally identified areas in the world to find areas meeting designer-defined criteria for dynamic encounters.
• General gameplay, optimizations and whatever else the game needed that I could help with.
positions.insights: Skills: Version Control · Skilled Multi-tasker · Critical Thinking · Optimization · Creative Ideation · Cross-functional Collaborations · Coaching · Technical Architecture

• Low level diagnostics for exotic, hard to solve bugs.

projects.title: Star Ninja
projects.description: A 2D physics based puzzle game that was released as a free and paid version for Windows Phone, and another version for the Xbox 360. This game has had over 400,000 downloads and consistently high reviews from the players.

projects.title: Untold Legends: Dark Kingdom
projects.description: Joined this team rather late to help complete the title in time for the Playstation 3 launch. Implemented support for audio hooks, voice chat, physics triggered sounds, script related sound controls and generally provided support for all things related to sound.

publications.title: Dynamic Space Partitioning, Reservation, and Player Movement For Concurrent, Non-linear and Virtual Location-based Entertainment

patents.title: System and method for regulating overlapping media messages
patents.description: The described systems regulate the transmission and playback of multiple streams of audio data, e.g., for a multiplayer game, and provide sequential playback of audio, buffered while the listener is listening to a different stream, time-compressed if necessary. The systems thus solve a problem of users 'talking over each other' by: (1) regulating access to audio channels; and (2) treating the spoken audio as distinct blocks so as to play the messages, e.g., from multiple channels, sequentially to users. The messages may be played back at a later time at time-compressed rates or aborted as directed by the user or by a separate automated process.
